title: A routine stall: the puck refills
note: v1.1 (M9): the player waits for 6 s of picture after every stall, so most .ts hiccups freeze for 6 s. While it's refilling at full speed the puck fills toward it (here 3.7 of 6 s); no card, no words.

title: Not recovering: checking
note: The card opens only when the refill is too slow to finish in time (SPEC 3.1). Each link fills with the pink progress as its check answers. ▲▼ Zap says he isn't stuck.

title: Cause: the provider is slow
note: Not you, them. One pair of numbers (3 of 9 Mbps); the internet just reads Fast (S2: the test can't see past about 60 Mbps). OK switches to the game's other feed, which keeps its own score delay. No score anywhere.

title: Cause: weak Wi-Fi
note: v1.1 (M3, S6): blamed on the Wi-Fi only when the bars, the TV's link speed and the speed test agree. Nothing past the bottleneck is ticked: it can't be judged. OK plays the provider's HD copy (live .ts has no 720p level).

title: Cause: slow internet
note: On a network cable, so it isn't Wi-Fi; the speed test (plus what the stream got in the same 3 s, S1) says the line is short. OK plays the HD copy (needs 9 Mbps).

title: Cause: home network or line, can't split
note: v1.1 (M3): strong bars and a fast Wi-Fi link, but a slow test: busy airwaves or the line itself, which a TV can't tell apart. Both links get the "!"; Details says how a cable would tell (SPEC 4.1 C3h).

title: Wi-Fi dropped, picture still playing
note: v1.1 (S15): the network went but there's still picture in hand. A chip, no action, no countdown; it goes when the network's back, and turns into the card only if the picture actually stops.

title: Cause: the TV is offline
note: The picture has stopped and Android says there is no network: no checks. It tunes again once the network has been back and working for 2 s (S8).

title: Cause: the provider isn't answering
note: v1.1 (M1, M2): "Provider" is the server the stream really comes from (after redirects). Only that server failing its own check, with the Wi-Fi fine, makes this card; a timeout on weak Wi-Fi is the Wi-Fi card.

title: Cause: this TV's last stream still counted
note: v1.1 (M5): a limit answer within 60 s of this TV closing a stream is this TV's own old stream. airglow backs off 10, 20, 30 s; "by other devices" only if the count stays full after that.

title: Keeps pausing: the chip
note: v1.1 (S12): the kit's chip exactly (8 s, max 420), one line of cause. "Your team is live" wins the slot; this one waits, or is dropped after 30 s.

title: A movie: slow internet
note: Movies and episodes: the last node reads Movie. A film can wait, so the best action is to pause and load ahead (next mock). With the controls up, OK stays play/pause and the card shows no keys (S13).

title: A movie: loading ahead
note: v1.1 (M10): paused by this action, the player lets the buffer grow far past its usual 50 s (to disk). The line says what the loaded part is worth, not just its length: loaded ÷ (1 − 7/16).

title: Stopped: the channel is off
note: v1.1 (S5): a 404 twice while the stream's own server answers. A stale channel list is a common reason on Xtream, so Refresh channels is one row down.

title: Stopped: a game feed is off
note: A game channel: the other feeds first, one OK away; each keeps its own score delay. No score or clock. v1.1: titles without "US:".

title: Stopped: the TV can't decode it
note: v1.1 (M4, S17): only a format beyond the TV (checked against its decoder table), or a decoder that fails twice. The ticks stand: the picture's data arrived through every link. No codec names.

title: Stopped: the picture is broken at the source
note: v1.1 (M4): DECODING_FAILED on a format inside the TV's decoder table is the stream, not the TV.

title: Options: the Connection row
note: ◀ in the player, any time. Connection sits under Quality; its value is the live verdict, its line the one number that matters ("about": a .ts stream doesn't say its rate, S4).

title: Options while the card shows
note: v1.1 (S10): Hold OK stays Last channel. Details is ◀ then OK: while a card or chip shows, Options opens with Connection first and focused, then Other feeds.

title: The Connection panel: all good
note: Options > Connection. "Checked" is the time of the last check, not of opening. 60+: the test's ceiling (S2). Provider is the stream's own server (M1).

title: The Connection panel: during the stall
note: v1.1 (M8, S6): .ts-real actions only (another feed, another copy, try again; no "other stream type"). "1 s ahead" moved to the problem row, so the TV's tick means only what was checked.

title: Account: Check the connection
note: Account > Provider gets one row under Check the guide. v1.1: the rows end at x 906 so the ring stays inside the safe line.

title: The check, running
note: OK on the row: the five links in order, about 10 s. Nothing to press while it runs; Back stops it.

title: The check: all good
note: The verdict in what it means for him (4K, HD). The last channel is sampled for 5 s only on a 2+ stream account, and "done" waits until the provider has let the stream go (S14).

title: The check: Wi-Fi is the limit
note: v1.1 (M3): blamed on the Wi-Fi because three readings agree (1 bar, a 26 Mbps link, a 14 Mbps test near it). The internet past it isn't judged; the provider and the channel were checked directly.
